reasons: The behaviour checks are clear, but no test run result was provided.
The source scan is a pattern match and can miss other forms.

terms.meaning: Time to live: how long a cache entry stays fresh before it expires.
Least recently used: the rule that removes the entry no one has looked at for the longest time when the cache is full.
A variable declared at the top of a file, which lives as long as the program runs.

used_by: Run by the test runner as part of the unit tests.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup
sections.what: Imports the file reading tools, the test runner and the cache classes.
sections.why: Gives the tests what they need to check the cache and scan the code.

sections.name: clock
sections.title: Fake clock
sections.what: Creates a clock that the test sets by hand, so time moves only when the test says so.
sections.why: Makes expiry tests exact and repeatable.
sections.watch_out: Tests do not use the real clock, so a bug in real timing would not show here.

sections.name: cache: keyed, bounded TTL cache
sections.title: Cache behaviour and code scan
sections.what: Checks that entries expire after their time limit but can still be read as stale with their age, that keys are separate, that the cache keeps only a set number of entries and drops the least recently used one, that zero or unlimited settings are refused, that named caches are shared by name, and that no module-level cache variables appear in the app, domain, library or component folders.
sections.why: Likely reason: cached data must not leak between users or stay around unexpectedly in a long-running server.
sections.watch_out: The scan matches only a specific declaration pattern, so a cache written in a different style would pass.

summary: Tests the small in-memory cache: how long entries live, how keys and sizes are limited, how named caches are shared, and that no shared cache variables remain in app code.
purpose: Keeps the cache behaving predictably and prevents a common mistake of keeping shared data in module-level variables.
why: Likely reason: module-level caches can keep data across requests or users, so the rule is enforced by a scan of the code.
how: Uses a fake clock to move time forward by hand. Checks expiry, stale reads, key separation, size limits with least-recently-used removal, refusal of bad settings, named cache sharing, and a scan of the app folders for forbidden cache variables.
inputs: Simple keys and values written in tests, a fake clock, and the source files of the app.
risks: The source scan only spots let or var declarations, so a cache written another way passes. Expiry is tested only through the fake clock.
debug: If expiry fails, check the time values set on the fake clock. If the source scan fails, the message names the file with a cache variable.
